properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The one place the vocabulary genuinely strains against a plan. reflow2's temporal axis is DECISION time — DesignEpoch, Snapshot, valid_from/valid_to, ChangeEvent: "when did we settle this, and what was in force then". A plan needs EXECUTION time: H-hour and offsets from it, durations, windows, and a critical path computed from dependencies. Flow + PRECEDES + TRIGGERS gives ordering, not schedule. (a) ADD IT — scheduled instants/durations on Flow steps plus a computed critical path; the biggest vocabulary addition since the temporal axis, and it makes "the timeline slipped" a computation rather than a note. (b) LEAVE IT OUT and reference an external schedule (MS Project, a synch matrix) from the graph; keeps reflow2 out of a crowded, well-solved problem, at the cost that the blast radius of a slip cannot be computed — which is exactly the thing worth having. (c) MINIMAL — offsets from a named reference event and durations, no calendar, no resource levelling, no Gantt: enough to compute what a slip breaks, not enough to be a scheduling tool. THE VOCABULARY CONSTRAINT EITHER WAY: no military or acquisition words enter the schema (req:design-anything, and the way dec:mosa-conformance was settled) — H-hour is a named reference event, not a schema noun.
properties.name: OPEN — does reflow2 model scheduled time (H-hour, durations, critical path) as a first-class axis?
properties.rationale: Named as the honest gap while mapping a staff planning process onto the existing vocabulary, which otherwise carried it almost without strain: ALLOCATED_TO is troop-to-task, Interface plus PROVIDES/CONSUMES is a coordination point or transfer of authority, Decision plus register_alternative is COA development and comparison, Constraint is constraints and restraints with breach computed, Verification is a rehearsal or confirmation brief, and a FRAGO is a ChangeEvent with a computed blast radius. Recorded rather than acted on because (c) is a real design choice that turns on whether any computation would read it — the same test dec:exploratory-staging applies to brainstorm vocabulary — and because getting it wrong means either reimplementing MS Project badly or leaving the highest-value computation on the table. Detail in docs/planning-at-scale.md §1.
